options.label: Biological sciences: cells, organisms and ecosystems
options.labelReason: The programme spans biological organisation from molecules and cells through physiology, organisms, biodiversity and ecosystems, supported by laboratory, statistical and data methods.
options.concept: Study life from genes and cells to organisms and ecosystems. Connect biochemistry, physiology and disease to evolution, conservation and marine ecology. Use laboratory methods, programming and statistics to investigate biological questions.
progression: The life science gateway precedes dependent courses. Programming precedes data science, and Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics. Introductory biodiversity precedes ecology, conservation and evolution.

options.label: Molecular, cellular and biomedical biology
options.labelReason: Molecular-cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, immunology, physiology and experimental/data methods form a coherent health-facing biological direction supported by the programme’s cells, genomics, bioinformatics, neurobiology and health interests.
options.concept: Study how cells, genes and biomolecules shape health and disease. Use laboratory methods, anatomy, physiology and neuroscience to investigate mechanisms, then apply statistics, epidemiology and computing to health evidence and biological data.
progression: The life science and brain gateways precede dependent courses. Molecular cell biology comes before molecular pathology and disease. Programming and mathematics come before applied data science, and data science precedes machine learning and deep learning.
options.distinctness: This option shares molecular, physiological and evolutionary foundations with the broad option. It uses seven different courses to develop neuroscience, epidemiology and computational prediction and imaging in place of several ecology and environmental courses.

options.label: Ecology, evolution and conservation biology
options.labelReason: Evolution, biodiversity, ecosystems, conservation, climate, biogeochemistry and field-oriented environmental research form a coherent direction grounded in explicit programme interests and current Biology study-interest guidance.
options.concept: Study how evolution and environmental change shape biodiversity. Connect conservation, marine ecology and farming to climate, soils and nutrient cycles. Use field, laboratory and statistical methods and investigate a sustainability question with a regional partner.
progression: Early biodiversity and sustainability courses support later marine ecology, conservation and biogeochemistry. The life science gateway precedes the dependent cell biology, laboratory, physiology and immunity courses. The regional partner project runs in term one and introduces guided team research.
options.distinctness: This option adds eight courses to the broad option in sustainability systems, climate, farming, Earth-system methods, biogeochemistry and regional partner research. It focuses on populations, habitats and environmental change instead of concentrating on human disease and computing.

analysis: The broad option has credible biological breadth in cellular mechanisms, organismal physiology, evolution, conservation, ecosystem dynamics and marine ecology. Biochemistry and molecular pathology explain molecular processes, Life Science Laboratory supplies microbiology, protein and DNA work, and probability, calculus and data analysis provide methods. Soils, hazards and governance add applied context. The molecular option replaces natural hazards with evolutionary genetics and replaces Psycholinguistics with epidemiological study design, risk and causal appraisal. Molecular Cell Biology precedes pathology and disease, and the data sequence proceeds from programming and statistics through data handling, machine learning and deep learning. Neurobiology, perception and higher-order functions build a bounded biological neuroscience line. Image analysis applies to microscopy and anatomical images as a method. General computing does not substitute for a genomics or bioinformatics course. Ecology retains laboratory, physiology, microbial and evolutionary grounding and develops conservation, ocean ecosystems and the relationship of soils and nutrients to habitats. Dynamic Earth, the sustainability gateways, climate, soil methods, farming and biogeochemistry contribute to environmental context and enquiry. The partner project is guided team research with a topic dependent on the brief. The environmental hazards and Earth System Science Tools descriptions support concrete risk and modelling contributions, while Perception & Action supports neural mechanisms of sensory processing and action. Rhetoric in Action provides genuine instruction and feedback with primary pupils. Its rhetorical teaching and the broader communication offerings do not establish sustained Biology didactics or supervised secondary-school practice.

candidateDecisions.label: Educational minor in biology teaching
candidateDecisions.reason: Rhetoric in Action develops lesson design and coaching through speaking work with primary-school pupils. This is useful teaching practice. The available communication and biology courses lack a sustained biology-specific teaching sequence with supervised secondary-school practice. The two selected directions have stronger disciplinary coverage.

alignment.rationale: Both examine cellular structure, gene expression, signalling and molecular mechanisms. UCR’s separate life science gateway supplies the introductory foundation.
Both introduce evolution and biodiversity across major groups of life.
Both address animal structure and function; UCR concentrates on human physiology.
Both study microorganisms. UCR emphasises infection and immune responses. Its biodiversity course surveys plant diversity, while Utrecht includes dedicated plant physiology.
Both combine ecological principles with modelling or experimental reasoning.
Both study genes and genomes. UCR emphasises inheritance, mutations and disease. Utrecht gives dedicated attention to genome analysis.
Utrecht requires one of two first-year Biology electives.
Students choose these courses from the Biology major list subject to level and course-entry rules.
Both develop quantitative biological reasoning and statistics; UCR supplies a general mathematical-statistics sequence.
Utrecht requires a dedicated academic communication course. UCR develops related writing and presentation skills across courses.

Utrecht requires supervised biological research, a written report and a presentation. The ecology option includes a team partner project whose topic depends on the brief. UCR offers optional independent research separately.
Utrecht reserves 45 EC for profiling through electives or a minor.
